in_urdu.name: انار
in_urdu.meaning: رمان کا پھل، انار کا پھل
in_urdu.long_meaning: انار ایک خوبصورت اور لذیذ پھل ہے، جو جنوبی ایشیا میں بہت مقبول ہے، انار کی جڑیں العربية ہیں، اور اس کا ذکر قرآن مجید میں بھی ہوا ہے، یہ پھل صحت، خوشبختی اور کثرت کی علامت ہے

in_hindi.name: अनार

in_pashto.name: انار

historical_references.reference: Anar was a renowned Sufi saint and poet from the 13th century Persia. He is also known as Anar Shah or Anar Khodawandi. Anar is believed to have been born in the village of Anarbad in the present-day Afghan province of Herat, and spent his life studying and teaching in various Sufi centers across Persia and India. Anar's poetry reflects the deep spiritual and mystical aspects of Sufism, and his works have had a profound impact on Sufi literature and music.
historical_references.context: Sufi saint and poet, born in Persia, studied and taught in various Sufi centers across Persia and India.

historical_references.reference: Anar was a Persian princess and wife of Prophet Muhammad's cousin and companion, Ali ibn Abi Talib. She is also known as Umm al-Banin or Umm al-Husain. Anar is believed to have been born in Medina around 600 CE and was married to Ali around 622 CE. She is known for her piety and generosity, and is revered as a saint in Shia Islam. Anar is believed to have interceded on behalf of her husband and children during the Battle of the Camel, and her tomb is a popular pilgrimage site in Najaf, Iraq.
